title: Docker CopyEscape Vulnerability Lets Containers Write Outside Intended Host Paths
content_md: A high-severity Docker vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-17106, dubbed CopyEscape , can allow a malicious container to create or overwrite files outside the local destination specified in a docker cp command. The flaw affects the container-to-host copy workflow and can lead to code execution with the permissions of the user or automation process running the Docker CLI. Imperva Red Team researcher Ron Masas discovered the issue in Docker’s archive-handling pipeline. Rather than copying files directly from a container filesystem to a host path, docker cp causes the Docker daemon to package the requested container path into a tar archive. Docker CopyEscape Vulnerability The Docker CLI then extracts that archive onto the local system. CopyEscape abuses the trust boundary between the attacker-controlled container filesystem and the host-side extraction process. The attack combines a time-of-check/time-of-use race in archive creation with unsafe symlink handling during extraction. Architecture (Source: imperva) A process inside a running malicious container can alter filesystem objects while Docker is building the tar archive. Specifically, it can cause an archive to represent a pathname first as a directory and later as a symlink. When the Docker CLI extracts a subsequent child entry through that symlink, the write can be redirected outside the user-selected destination directory.
